title: Band slang, nicknames and the Hawk
summary: Albert explains the band's private language, the mysterious Hawk who took clothes, price signals and nicknames; the tape ends.

blocks.x: Your wife reminded us about Ben having her own language and chick keys and doing a restaurant.

Yeah, different things like that. And for instance, we would come to town and the menu had certain prices when it came for us to pay. It was a nickel, a dime, a quarter moment was on the menu. So you would ask the guy about that and you would tell you, well that's the end for the people in town. Out of town people had a different price. And then too we had the language of our own. We had the chick keys meant to stop talking, somebody was listening. Then we had the, what you call the hawk in the band. And then we had the, what you call the hawk. If you had a certain piece of clothing, a hat, a shirt, a tie or shoes that the hawk didn't like, it would come up missing. And nobody has ever been able to know who the hawk was. And we have tried to find out who the hawk was and nobody had ever found. We always suspected Geechee Robinson. But we never was able to pin it on him. But anything that wasn't liked about a hawk, it would come up missing.

Well, supposing some of the musicians would be talking about your coat or your tie. They'd say, watch it say the hawk's going to get it. They'd be having a cue to get hold of whatever it was, whoever the hawk was. I imagine somebody knew who the hawk was but they never knew. And then they used to call her, if a chick wasn't a nice looking chick, they would call her Taylor. And then she was not such a nice looking gal. What do you call her? Well, they call her a good looking chick. That's a nice looking Taylor. Oh, and if we went to a place and the prices were too high, some guy said, umbrella. Umbrella meant watch it because it wasn't right. And you would walk out. But it was all type of languages among, in the band. They had names. Everyone had a nickname. For instance, I was twenty years old. I was the old man. And then of course, Geechee, I told you, he was right. And then, uh, Albert Martin was called Fats. And of course, Nicky got his name, Nicky. Cottshell, we called him Bucks. Uh, Tunnel, we called him Nicodemus. Well, each individual had some sort of moniker tied onto his actual name. Nobody, nobody took an offense to it. Everybody was happy. It was just one of those things. Mm-hmm. And, uh, we always tried to remember these towns, these places that we had gone to, and we wouldn't frequent those places. We'd pass it by. Mm-hmm.
